author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of fleeing from vain hope and pride

verses.text: Vain is the life of that man who putteth his trust in men or in any created Thing.
verses.modernizedText: The life of a person who puts his trust in people or in any created thing is vain.

verses.text: Be not ashamed to be the servant of others for the love of Jesus Christ, and to be reckoned poor in this life.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be ashamed to serve others for the love of Jesus Christ and to be considered poor in this life.

verses.text: Rest not upon thyself, but build thy hope in God.
verses.modernizedText: Do not rest on yourself, but build your hope in God.

verses.text: Do what lieth in thy power, and God will help thy good intent.
verses.modernizedText: Do what is in your power, and God will help your good intention.

verses.text: Trust not in thy learning, nor in the cleverness of any that lives, but rather trust in the favour of God, who resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble.
verses.modernizedText: Do not trust in your learning or in the cleverness of anyone living, but trust instead in the favor of God, who resists the proud and gives grace to the humble.

verses.text: Boast not thyself in thy riches if thou hast them, nor in thy friends if they be powerful, but in God, who giveth all things, and in addition to all things desireth to give even Himself.
verses.modernizedText: Do not boast of your riches if you have them, or of your friends if they are powerful, but boast in God, who gives all things and, in addition to all things, desires to give even Himself.

verses.text: Be not lifted up because of thy strength or beauty of body, for with only a slight sickness it will fail and wither away.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be lifted up because of your bodily strength or beauty, for with only a slight sickness it will fail and wither away.

verses.text: Be not vain of thy skilfulness or ability, lest thou displease God, from whom cometh every good gift which we have.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be vain about your skill or ability, lest you displease God, from whom comes every good gift we have.

verses.text: Count not thyself better than others, lest perchance thou appear worse in the sight of God, who knoweth what is in man.
verses.modernizedText: Do not consider yourself better than others, lest you perhaps appear worse in the sight of God, who knows what is in a person.

verses.text: Be not proud of thy good works, for God’s judgments are of another sort than the judgments of man, and what pleaseth man is ofttimes displeasing to Him.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be proud of your good works, for God’s judgments are different from human judgments, and what pleases people is often displeasing to Him.

verses.text: If thou hast any good, believe that others have more, and so thou mayest preserve thy humility.
verses.modernizedText: If you have any good, believe that others have more, and so you may preserve your humility.

verses.text: It is no harm to thee if thou place thyself below all others; but it is great harm if thou place thyself above even one.
verses.modernizedText: It does you no harm to place yourself below all others, but it does great harm to place yourself above even one.

verses.text: Peace is ever with the humble man, but in the heart of the proud there is envy and continual wrath.
verses.modernizedText: Peace is always with the humble person, but in the heart of the proud there is envy and continual anger.
